fields.meta_title: Time Off Request Form That Checks Balances | Emergent
fields.meta_description: What to put on a time off request form, how to word the ask, and an app that checks PTO balances and shift cover before a manager approves.
fields.h1: Build a Time Off Request Form That Checks PTO Balances
fields.hero_description: A time off request form records the days an employee wants off and the hours they use. Describe your leave policy, and Emergent builds the form and its approvals.
fields.explore_cta: Build My Time Off Request Form
fields.features_heading: Your Leave Policy, Applied on Every Request
fields.features_subheading: A printable time off request form collects dates and a signature. Emergent's version checks the balance and the schedule first.
fields.feature_1:
Balance shown before submit

Shows the employee's remaining PTO hours next to the dates they pick, along with the hours the request would use. Anyone asking for more than they have sees the gap first.
fields.feature_2:
Minimum staffing per shift

Counts who is already off on each requested day against the minimum you set per role or location. A request that would leave a shift short reaches the manager as a conflict.
fields.feature_3:
Approvals in Slack or email

Sends each request to the employee's manager as a Slack message with approve and decline buttons. Anything left unanswered for two business days gets a reminder, then escalates.
fields.feature_4:
Leave types routed by policy

Routes vacation and personal days to the manager, and medical or family leave straight to HR. Managers see the dates someone is away, never the reason behind a medical request.
fields.feature_5:
Accrual tracked per pay period

Adds hours to each balance on the schedule your policy sets and caps carryover where you set a limit. Every change is stored in a database you own, ready for payroll to export.
fields.feature_6:
The code is yours to extend

Pushes the full codebase to your GitHub on paid plans. Your engineers can wire approved hours into a payroll provider's API, or ask Emergent to add that sync with one more prompt.

fields.usecase_heading: Time Off Request Forms by Type of Leave
fields.tab_content_1:
Saturday cover counted before anyone says yes

Retail schedules break on Saturdays. A cashier asks for one off, and the form checks who already has that day. Two of the five cashiers are out, and the store needs three on the floor. One more absence would leave two. The request reaches the store manager marked as a coverage conflict.
fields.tab_content_2:
Approve in Slack, see it on the team calendar

Most office requests are routine: three days off next month, plenty of notice, nobody else away. The manager gets a Slack message with the dates and the balance, then approves it in place. The days land on the team calendar, and the employee's balance drops to 56 hours, down 24 from 80.
fields.tab_content_3:
Medical leave goes to HR, not the manager

Medical leave is different. An employee who needs time to care for a parent picks family medical leave, and the request skips the manager. HR receives it with a countdown, because the FMLA eligibility notice is due within five business days. The manager's calendar shows the dates as away, with no reason attached.
fields.tab_content_4:
When a request runs past the balance

Balances run out before the year does. An employee with 4 hours of PTO left asks for 16 hours off, and the form shows that 12 of them would be unpaid before anything is sent. The manager approves the dates, HR signs off on the unpaid hours, and payroll receives them marked unpaid.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Time Off Request Form
fields.howto_description: A good request form is mostly policy written down. The seven steps start with the rules your managers already apply in their heads and end with the record payroll needs.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for exact dates and hours
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Put the balance on the form
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the policy: which leave types you offer, how hours accrue, how much notice each type needs and who approves it. A form can only enforce rules that exist somewhere outside a manager's memory.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the first and last day off, any partial days and the total hours charged. Hourly teams need shift times as well, because half a shift and half a day are rarely the same number of hours.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List vacation, sick, personal, bereavement, unpaid, and family medical leave as options instead of a free-text box. The type decides who approves the request and which balance it draws on. Leave the reason optional for vacation days.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Display the remaining balance beside the request and the hours it would use. When a request is bigger than the balance, say how many hours would go unpaid before the employee submits, not in a rejection a week later.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Set a minimum headcount for each shift or team and count approved absences against it. Requests that would drop a day below it go to the manager as conflicts. First-come approvals stop deciding who gets the holidays.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send any request that may qualify under the FMLA to HR instead of the manager. Federal rules give employers five business days to send the eligibility notice, and medical certifications belong in confidential files kept apart from personnel records.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Record who approved each request, when, and the balance before and after. Export approved hours to payroll each pay period. Keep denied requests too, with the reason the manager gave for each one.
